description.en: Réveillon, carols, bûche and reindeer: a festive lap around the world's Christmas traditions.
description.fr: Réveillon, chants, bûche et rennes : un tour du monde des traditions de Noël.
description.ar: ريفيون، أغاني، بوش دو نويل وغزلان الرنّة: جولة حول العالم بتقاليد الميلاد.
description.es: Cenas de Nochebuena, villancicos, turrón y renos: una vuelta al mundo por las tradiciones navideñas.

questions.text: In France, what is the big dinner on the night of 24 December called?
questions.explain: The word comes from 'réveiller', to wake up: the meal often goes on late into the night.

questions.text: The French Christmas cake called 'bûche de Noël' is shaped like…
questions.explain: It imitates the big log that families once burned in the hearth at Christmas.

questions.text: 'Silent Night' was first sung in 1818 in a village in which country?
questions.explain: At its first performance, in Oberndorf near Salzburg, it was accompanied on a guitar.

questions.text: In 'Home Alone' (1990), Kevin's family flies off without him to spend Christmas in which city?
questions.explain: The McCallisters live near Chicago; Kevin's mother finally makes it home on Christmas Day.

questions.text: Saint Nicholas, who inspired Santa Claus, lived in Myra. In which present-day country is it?
questions.explain: His legend of secret gift-giving became Sinterklaas in the Netherlands, then Santa Claus.

questions.text: Female reindeer grow antlers too.
questions.explain: They're the only deer whose females grow antlers; mothers usually keep theirs through the winter.

questions.text: Rovaniemi, in Finnish Lapland, calls itself Santa Claus's official hometown. Which line runs through its Santa Claus Village?
questions.explain: A line on the ground marks the Arctic Circle in the village square, so visitors can step across it.

questions.text: In Provence, how many desserts are traditionally laid out after the Christmas Eve supper?
questions.explain: They include the 'four beggars': dried figs, almonds, raisins, and walnuts or hazelnuts.

questions.text: Panettone, the tall Christmas bread with candied fruit and raisins, comes from which Italian city?
questions.explain: Its cousin pandoro, star-shaped and dusted with icing sugar, comes from Verona.

questions.text: Which band sang 'Last Christmas' in 1984?
questions.explain: It only reached No. 1 in the UK in January 2021, 36 years after its release.

questions.text: Which actor plays Buddy, the human raised by elves, in 'Elf' (2003)?
questions.explain: As a baby, Buddy crawled into Santa's sack at an orphanage and woke up at the North Pole.

questions.text: Coca-Cola invented Santa Claus's red suit.
questions.explain: Red-suited Santas existed long before; Coke's ads from 1931 mainly made that jolly look famous.

questions.text: What are wild reindeer called in North America?
questions.explain: Same species, two names: 'reindeer' in Europe, 'caribou' for the wild ones of North America.

questions.text: Since 1947, which city has sent London the big Christmas tree that stands in Trafalgar Square every year?
questions.explain: It is a Norway spruce, usually over 20 metres tall and 50 to 60 years old, picked from the forests around the city.

questions.text: In Sweden, what does the girl chosen as Lucia wear on her head on 13 December?
questions.explain: Lucia's day falls in the darkest weeks of the Nordic winter; today the candles are usually battery-powered.

questions.text: Spanish turrón, a Christmas sweet, is made mainly of…
questions.explain: Soft Jijona turrón uses ground almonds; hard Alicante turrón keeps them whole.

questions.text: Who sings 'All I Want for Christmas Is You' (1994)?
questions.explain: She wrote it with Walter Afanasieff; it was the lead single from her first Christmas album.

questions.text: Who created the Grinch, the green grump who tries to steal Christmas?
questions.explain: The Grinch grumbles that he has put up with Christmas for 53 years: Dr. Seuss's own age when the book came out, in 1957.

questions.text: Rudolph the red-nosed reindeer was created in 1939 for…
questions.explain: The Montgomery Ward stores handed out 2.4 million copies of his story in the first year.

questions.text: Reindeer eyes change colour with the seasons: golden in summer, and what colour in winter?
questions.explain: The change makes their eyes far more sensitive to light during the long polar night.

questions.text: Which French city, home to a Christmas market since 1570, calls itself the 'Capital of Christmas'?
questions.explain: Its Christkindelsmärik is the oldest Christmas market in France.

questions.text: In Mexico, how many nights do the 'Posadas' before Christmas last?
questions.explain: From 16 to 24 December: songs, candles, and a piñata to round off the evening.

questions.text: In Lebanon, 'burbara', made for Saint Barbara's Day, is mainly…
questions.explain: Legend says wheat fields grew around Barbara in no time to hide her.

questions.text: In December 1965, the Gemini 6 astronauts played which Christmas song in orbit, on a harmonica they had smuggled aboard?
questions.explain: It was the first time musical instruments were played in space; the harmonica and bells are now at the Smithsonian.

questions.text: In 'The Nightmare Before Christmas', Jack Skellington is the Pumpkin King of which town?
questions.explain: Chris Sarandon is his speaking voice; Danny Elfman sings his songs.

questions.text: Which royal made the Christmas tree fashionable in Britain, after an 1848 picture of the royal family around one?
questions.explain: The engraving appeared in the Illustrated London News and inspired households across the country.

questions.text: The poinsettia, the red 'Christmas star' plant, is native to which country?
questions.explain: Its red 'petals' are actually leaves called bracts; the real flowers are the tiny yellow buds in the middle.

questions.text: In Italy, who brings presents to children on the night of 5 January?
questions.explain: She's an old woman on a broomstick; tradition says naughty children get a lump of coal.

questions.text: British mince pies used to contain real meat.
questions.explain: Today's 'mincemeat' is dried fruit, apples and spices; only the name is left of the meat.

questions.text: Guinness lists 'White Christmas' as the best-selling single of all time. Who sang it?
questions.explain: Irving Berlin wrote it for the 1942 film Holiday Inn; it won the Oscar for best song.

questions.text: In 'It's a Wonderful Life' (1946), what happens 'every time a bell rings'?
questions.explain: Clarence, still without wings after 200 years, earns them by saving George Bailey.

questions.text: The first tinsel, made in Nuremberg around 1610, was made of real silver.
questions.explain: Silver tarnished quickly; today tinsel is mostly plastic film with a metallic coating.

questions.text: Mistletoe, hung up for the holidays in Britain and France, is…
options: A half-parasite that grows on trees
questions.explain: Birds spread its seeds in their droppings or by wiping their beaks on tree bark.

questions.text: In Spain, many children get their main presents on 6 January, from the Three Kings.
questions.explain: On the evening of 5 January, towns hold big parades for the Kings, called cabalgatas.

questions.text: In France, what is hidden inside a galette des rois in January?
questions.explain: Whoever finds it wears the paper crown and is king or queen for the day.

questions.text: 'Petit Papa Noël' (1946), the best-selling single ever in France, was a hit for which singer?
questions.explain: Guinness estimates it has sold about 5.7 million copies in France alone.

questions.text: 'Klaus' (2019), the Oscar-nominated animated film about how Santa Claus began, was made in which country?
questions.explain: It was the first animated Christmas film nominated for the Oscar for best animated feature.

questions.text: In 1882, the first electrically lit Christmas tree glowed in New York, at the home of a partner of which inventor?
questions.explain: Edward Johnson wired 80 red, white and blue bulbs by hand; the tree even turned on its stand.

questions.text: How many sides does a snowflake have?
questions.explain: Water molecules freeze into hexagonal rings, which gives every snowflake its six-fold symmetry.

questions.text: According to Dutch tradition, Sinterklaas arrives in mid-November by steamboat from which country?
questions.explain: Once ashore, he rides through the streets on his horse; the arrival is broadcast live on Dutch TV.

questions.text: In Portugal, what is the classic dish of the Christmas Eve supper (the consoada)?
questions.explain: Portugal is the world's biggest eater of bacalhau: around six kilos per person a year.

questions.text: Who wrote and sang 'Feliz Navidad' in 1970?
questions.explain: The Puerto Rican singer sings it in Spanish and English, and plays a Puerto Rican cuatro on it.

questions.text: Where does the cult French comedy 'Le Père Noël est une ordure' (1982) take place?
questions.explain: It is set on Christmas Eve and was adapted from a 1979 play by the Splendid comedy troupe.

questions.text: In which country did the custom of the decorated Christmas tree begin?
questions.explain: A record from Bremen in 1570 describes a tree hung with apples, nuts, dates, pretzels and paper flowers.

questions.text: Polar bears and penguins can meet in the wild.
questions.explain: Polar bears live in the Arctic; almost all wild penguins live in the southern hemisphere.

questions.text: In Icelandic folklore, how many 'Yule Lads' visit children in the days before Christmas?
questions.explain: Children leave a shoe on the windowsill: a small gift for the good ones, a potato for the naughty.

questions.text: Fairuz sings a famous Arabic Christmas song set to the tune of which carol?
options: We Wish You a Merry Christmas
questions.explain: In her version, the snow and sleighs give way to warm homes full of decorations and ringing bells.

questions.text: Who wrote 'A Christmas Carol', the story of the miser Ebenezer Scrooge?
questions.explain: Published in December 1843, it sold out before Christmas Eve and has never been out of print.

questions.text: In Australia, Christmas falls in the middle of winter.
questions.explain: December is summer south of the equator: the shortest day up north is the longest day down there.

questions.text: In Japan, eating KFC fried chicken at Christmas is a popular tradition.
questions.explain: It took off with a 1974 advertising campaign: 'Kentucky for Christmas'.

questions.text: How old was Brenda Lee when she recorded 'Rockin' Around the Christmas Tree' in 1958?
questions.explain: In December 2023, 65 years later, the song finally reached No. 1 in the United States.

questions.text: In the northern hemisphere, the shortest day of the year falls around…
questions.explain: After the winter solstice, the days slowly start getting longer again.

questions.text: In Lebanon, what do children traditionally do on Saint Barbara's night, around 4 December?
options: Dress up and go door to door
questions.explain: The custom recalls the legend of Barbara, who hid under many disguises.

questions.text: The Nutcracker ballet was a big hit from its very first night, in Saint Petersburg in 1892.
questions.explain: Critics panned the premiere; the full ballet only became a Christmas classic decades later.

questions.text: Which country is known for the world's longest Christmas season, starting in September?
questions.explain: Filipinos call them the 'ber months': as soon as September begins, the Christmas songs start.

questions.text: In Catalonia, the 'Tió de Nadal' that 'gives' sweets to children at Christmas is…
questions.explain: Children 'feed' it for weeks, then tap it with sticks while singing until it gives up its treats.

questions.text: In Poland, what does the Christmas Eve supper (Wigilia) traditionally wait for before it begins?
options: The first star in the sky
questions.explain: An extra place is also set at the table for an unexpected guest.

questions.text: What do you traditionally find inside a British Christmas cracker?
options: A paper crown and a joke
questions.explain: Crackers were invented by the London confectioner Tom Smith in the 1840s.

questions.text: In Lebanon, what do children usually call the old man in red who brings the presents?
questions.explain: The name comes from French; some also say 'Baba Noël'.

questions.text: In Colombia, the Christmas season traditionally opens on the night of 7 December with…
questions.explain: It's the 'Día de las Velitas', the Day of the Little Candles, lit in houses and streets alike.
